Dear Ms. Alvarez,

I am writing to take full responsibility for the data entry error that occurred in last week's financial report. After reviewing the situation carefully, I want to acknowledge my mistake and explain the steps I have taken to ensure it does not happen again.

The error occurred when I failed to double-check figures before submitting the final version of the report. At the time, I was confident that the information was accurate; however, I later discovered inconsistencies that affected the overall analysis. I understand that this mistake caused confusion and required additional time for correction, and I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience it created for the team.

Rather than making excuses, I believe it is important to focus on accountability and improvement. Immediately after identifying the issue, I notified the relevant team members and worked overtime to correct the data. I also reviewed our internal procedures to better understand where my process fell short.

As a result, I have implemented several changes to my workflow. I now use a verification checklist before submitting any reports and schedule additional time for peer review when possible. I have also requested access to further training to strengthen my attention to detail and improve my understanding of financial compliance standards.

This experience has reinforced an important lesson about professionalism. Mistakes are sometimes unavoidable, but how they are handled defines one's reliability and integrity. By addressing the issue promptly and transparently, I hope to rebuild trust and demonstrate my commitment to high-quality work.

Thank you for your understanding and for giving me the opportunity to correct this mistake. I value my role within the organization and remain dedicated to contributing positively moving forward.

Respectfully,
Sophia Nguyen
